articles.headline: OFAC Designates Guatemalan Drug Trafficking Organizations for Narcotics and Terrorism
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has designated several Guatemalan drug trafficking organizations (DTOs) under counter-narcotics and counter-terrorism authorities. The designations target Los Lorenzanas, Los Mendoza Drug Trafficking Organization, and Los Huistas Drug Trafficking Organization, exposing them to secondary sanctions risk under Executive Order 13224, as amended by Executive Order 13886.

Los Lorenzanas has been identified as a transnational terrorist group, while Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO are linked to Mexican cartels, including the Sinaloa Cartel and the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG). These groups allegedly control key trafficking corridors along Guatemala's borders with Mexico and Honduras, providing logistical and financial support to their Mexican counterparts.

The action aims to disrupt the financial channels and networks supporting these illicit activities, extending the reach of U.S. sanctions to non-U.S. parties dealing with the designated organizations. This move underscores the U.S. government's commitment to combating transnational organized crime and its ties to terrorism.

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran-Related SDN Listing for Volta Shipping Services
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued an update to an Iran-related listing on its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List. The update pertains to Volta Shipping Services LLC, a UAE-based company previously linked to Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani.

The administrative change amends the company's listed alias from Volta Shipping Services FZCO to Volta Container Line FZCO. Despite the alias change, Volta Shipping Services LLC remains designated under Executive Order 13902 and continues to be subject to secondary sanctions risk.

This update is part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to maintain the accuracy and effectiveness of its sanctions lists, ensuring that entities involved in illicit activities related to Iran are properly identified and targeted.

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Eight Canadian Money Services Businesses Tied to Iranian Sanctions Evasion
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has designated eight Canada-based money services businesses (MSBs) for facilitating transactions involving Iran. This action, part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targets international financial channels used by Iran to evade sanctions.

These MSBs are accused of converting Iranian currency into digital assets and conducting transactions with sanctioned Iranian exchanges and digital asset addresses linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The designations were made under Executive Order 13902.

The action was coordinated with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and Canada's Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre (FINTRAC), highlighting international cooperation in combating illicit financial activities that support the Iranian regime.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cuban and Chinese Entities, Expands Sanctions to Key Cuban Economic Sectors
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting Cuban oil shippers, Cuban state entities, and Chinese military suppliers. Concurrently, OFAC issued a determination extending Executive Order 14404 to four additional sectors of the Cuban economy: manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine.

Among the designated entities are China National Electronic Import and Export Company (CEIEC) and Beijing H&C Technologies Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation. Both Chinese companies are accused of supplying equipment to Cuba's military through a Cuban arms procurement entity.

This action aims to further restrict the Cuban regime's access to resources and its ability to support hostile anti-American actors. The expansion of sanctions to new economic sectors means that companies and individuals operating in these areas could face future designations.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Shadow Fleet Network, Issues Alert, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations, targeting a network involved in supporting Iran's 'shadow fleet' and its efforts to evade sanctions. This action is part of 'Operation Economic Outcast' and aims to disrupt illicit maritime activities.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC published an Iran-related alert titled 'Iranian Shadow Fleet Reliance on False Flags for Sanctions Evasion,' warning of deceptive practices used to conceal the origin of Iranian oil. Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question.

The designations include four individuals and nine entities allegedly linked to an India-based network providing false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels transporting Iranian petroleum. OFAC also updated certain Iran-related listings and added a secondary sanctions risk notation to over 1,000 existing SDN entries, primarily those designated under Executive Order 13902.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran General License FF-1 for Wind Down of Transactions
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Iran General License FF-1, titled 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.' This amended general license provides authorization for certain wind-down activities.

The issuance of this general license is part of OFAC's ongoing management of its sanctions programs, allowing for an orderly cessation of transactions with specific entities. Such licenses are crucial for ensuring that U.S. persons and entities can comply with sanctions while minimizing undue disruption.

Parties involved in transactions with the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance should review the terms of General License FF-1 carefully to ensure compliance with the authorized wind-down period and activities.

body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting entities and individuals related to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. These actions aim to counter illicit activities and human rights abuses in these regions.

The specific details of the designations, including the identities of the sanctioned parties and the nature of their illicit activities, are available on OFAC's website. These designations typically involve asset freezes and prohibitions on transactions with U.S. persons.
These measures underscore the U.S. government's commitment to using sanctions as a tool to address national security and foreign policy concerns globally.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a $1,529,685 settlement with Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-headquartered cloud networking solutions provider. The settlement resolves nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks exported networking equipment and services to Joint Stock Company (JSC) Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer. MMZA was blocked by operation of law due to its majority ownership by designated entity JSC Concern Almaz Antey, even before its independent designation in 2022.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were voluntarily self-disclosed and egregious. The settlement amount reflects mitigating factors, including Extreme Networks' lack of prior OFAC enforcement history and its implementation of substantial remedial measures, such as enhanced screening procedures and increased employee training. The Department of Justice also announced a parallel non-prosecution agreement with Extreme Networks.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has amended 11 Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) related to blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC. This update is part of OFAC's ongoing process to ensure its published guidance remains current and clear.

The amended FAQs (10, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53) provide updated guidance on various aspects, including when to block or reject a payment, the calculation of interest on blocked funds, and the procedures for reporting blocked property and rejected transactions.

A significant change is the explicit instruction for all reports, including initial blocked property reports and annual reports, to be filed through the OFAC Reporting System (ORS) within ten business days of the relevant blocking or rejection. The updated guidance also clarifies the required supporting documentation for these reports.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran and Russia General Licenses, Amends FAQs, and Updates Sanctions Lists
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations, alongside removals of designations for Belarus and North Korea. Additionally, OFAC issued new general licenses related to Iran and Russia, and amended several Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

The Iran-related designations target entities and individuals involved in illicit activities supporting the Iranian regime. Concurrently, OFAC issued two Iran-related general licenses authorizing certain wind-down and other limited transactions involving recently blocked persons and vessels.

For Russia, a new general license was issued authorizing certain transactions involving the potential sale of Lukoil International GmbH. OFAC also amended two Russia-related FAQs and updated its Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List. The removals for Belarus and North Korea reflect specific policy considerations.

articles.headline: EU Imposes New Sanctions on 113 Russian Individuals and Entities, Targets Banking and Energy Sectors
body: The Council of the European Union has imposed additional restrictive measures on 12 individuals and 101 entities in response to Russia's ongoing aggression against Ukraine. This latest package of sanctions targets economic sectors that provide substantial revenue to Russia's war effort and support its 'shadow fleet.'

The new listings include nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions, aiming to further cut off financial channels that fund Russia's military. The sanctions also target individuals and entities in the Russian oil and energy sector, including those managing refineries and the St. Petersburg oil terminal.

Furthermore, the EU has targeted Russia's 'shadow fleet' by listing companies from the United Arab Emirates, China, the Seychelles, and Oman involved in purchasing Russian crude oil products, as well as businesspersons owning or managing vessels engaged in illegal transport of Russian oil. The package also includes the sole shareholder of Russian retail giant Wildberries and an individual controlling a majority stake in Ozon, another major Russian e-commerce company.

articles.headline: EU Sanctions 30 Individuals and Two Entities for Russia's FIMI and Malicious Cyber Activities
body: The Council of the European Union has decided to add 30 individuals and two entities to its list of those subject to EU restrictive measures, targeting Russia's foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI) and malicious cyber activities. This action is part of the EU's response to Russia's escalating and reckless behavior.

Among the newly listed entities is the Social Design Agency (SDA), a Moscow-based public relations and political technology company accused of carrying out large-scale information manipulation and interference projects funded and supervised by the Russian Presidential Administration.

Those subjected to these restrictive measures face an asset freeze and travel bans within the EU. Additionally, EU citizens and companies are prohibited from making funds available to them, directly or indirectly. This brings the total number of individuals and entities listed under this regime to 111 and 21, respectively.

articles.headline: EU Adds Gaza Now and Founder to Sanctions List Targeting Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad
body: The European Council has added the social media news outlet Gaza Now and its founder, Mustafa Moin Ayash, to the EU sanctions list targeting Hamas and the Palestinian Islamic Jihad. This action is part of the EU's framework against those who support, facilitate, or enable the violent actions of these organizations.
With these additions, a total of 22 individuals and four entities are now designated under the EU sanctions framework against Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad.

Those listed under this sanctions regime are subject to an asset freeze, and it is prohibited to provide them with funds or economic resources. A travel ban to the EU also applies to the natural persons named in the listing.

articles.headline: UK Adds 20 Entities to Sanctions List Under Russia Regime, Imposes Transport Sanctions
body: On November 12, 2026, the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) updated the UK Sanctions List on GOV.UK with 20 additions and one variation under the Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019. These new designations include JSC NIPIGAZPERERABOTKA (NIPIGAZ).

The newly added entities are now subject to asset freezes, trust services sanctions, and director disqualification sanctions. Notably, transport sanctions have also been imposed, prohibiting ships and aircraft owned, controlled, chartered, or operated by designated persons from entering or overflying the UK.

These transport sanctions also include prohibitions on providing technical assistance related to aircraft or ships to, or for the benefit of, the designated persons. The UK government considers there are reasonable grounds to suspect that NIPIGAZ is an involved person under the Russia sanctions regulations.

articles.headline: UN Security Council Reapplies Iran Sanctions Measures
body: On September 27, 2025, the United Nations Security Council's Iran measures were reapplied, effectively undoing the relief previously provided by resolution 2231. This action signifies a significant shift in the international approach to sanctions against Iran.
The reapplication of these measures means that a broader range of restrictions on dealings with Iran, its government, its banks, and listed persons are now in effect under UN authority.
This development impacts global compliance requirements for entities engaging with Iran, as UN sanctions are universally binding on member states.

body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle its potential civil liability for nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations. The violations involved the export of networking equipment and services to a Russian defense manufacturer.

The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) determined that between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks conducted transactions with Joint Stock Company (JSC) Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer. MMZA was blocked by operation of law due to its majority ownership by a designated entity, JSC Concern Almaz Antey.

OFAC considered the apparent violations to be voluntarily self-disclosed and egregious. The settlement amount reflects various mitigating factors, including the company's cooperation and remedial actions taken to enhance its sanctions compliance program.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
